{{Short description|Error-correcting codes used on compact discs}}
{{Cleanup|reason=This article doesn't really go into the function CIRC does and instead|date=January 2025}}
In the [[compact disc]] system, '''cross-interleaved Reed–Solomon code''' ('''CIRC''') provides error detection and [[error correction]].<ref>{{Patent|US|4413340|Inventors: Odaka K., Sako Y., Iwamoto I., Doi T.; Vries L.B.; SONY: ''Error correctable data transmission method'' (CIRC Patent) filing date May 21, 1980}}</ref> CIRC adds to every three data [[byte]]s one [[redundancy (information theory)|redundant]] [[parity bit|parity]] byte.

==Overview==
[[Reed–Solomon code]]s are specifically useful in combating mixtures of random and burst [[error]]s. CIRC corrects [[error burst]]s up to 4000 data bits in sequence (2.5&nbsp;mm in length as seen on CD surface) and compensates for error bursts up to 12,000 bits (7.5&nbsp;mm) that may be caused by minor scratches.<ref name="WickerBhargava1999">{{cite book|author=K.A.S. Immink|author-link=Kees Immink|editor=Stephen B. Wicker, Vijay K. Bhargava|title=Reed-Solomon Codes and Their Applications|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=yws55Rx1orEC&pg=PA41|date=12 October 1999|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=978-0-7803-5391-6|pages=41–59|chapter=Reed–Solomon Codes and the Compact Disc}}</ref>

==Characteristics==
* High random error correctability
* Long burst error correctability
* In case the burst correction capability is exceeded, [[interpolation]] may provide concealment by approximation
* Simple decoder strategy possible with reasonably-sized external [[random access memory]]
* Very high efficiency
* Room for future introduction of four audio channels without major changes in the format (as of 2024, this has not been implemented).

==Interleave==
Errors found in [[compact disc]]s (CDs) are a combination of random and burst errors. In order to alleviate the strain on the error control code, some form of interleaving is required. The CD system employs two [[concatenate]]d Reed–Solomon codes, which are [[forward error correction#Interleaving|interleaved cross-wise]]. Judicious positioning of the [[stereophonic sound|stereo]] channels as well as the audio samples on even or odd-number instants within the interleaving scheme, provide the error concealment ability, and the multitude of interleave structures used on the CD makes it possible to correct and detect errors with a relatively low amount of redundancy.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.usna.edu/Users/math/wdj/_files/documents/reed-sol.htm |title=Stan Hanley, Reed-Solomon Codes and CD Encoding |access-date=June 10, 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180917213045/https://www.usna.edu/Users/math/wdj/_files/documents/reed-sol.htm |archive-date=September 17, 2018 |url-status=bot: unknown }}</ref>
